idiom_name: named parameter idiom: RequestBuilder& method(...) { ...; return *this; } plus build()
implementation_notes: C++ cannot name or default constructor arguments at the call site, so the builder is written by hand as a fluent class or struct: one setter per optional field returning *this by lvalue reference (an &&-qualified overload returning std::move(*this) lets a temporary be consumed instead of copied), and build() validating cross-field rules and moving the accumulated state into the product. Since C++20 the builder is unnecessary for aggregates with in-class member initializers - designated initializers (.host = "api", .port = 443) give the same named, partial, defaulted construction with no boilerplate - so keep the classic form as soon as validation, resource acquisition or step ordering is involved.
pitfalls: A setter declared to return the builder by value copies the whole accumulated state on every chain step; return *this by reference, or std::move(*this) from an &&-qualified overload.
build() that moves out of the builder leaves a valid-but-unspecified object, so a named builder must not be reused afterwards; provide reset() or a fresh builder per product.
Without a validation step a required field still holding its in-class default silently produces a wrong object: the code compiles and the mistake appears only at runtime.

variants.name: Generated message accumulator (Protocol Buffers)
variants.idiom_name: generated protobuf message as mutable accumulator: Foo::set_* / add_* / mutable_* then copy or move
variants.implementation_notes: Protocol Buffers' C++ generator does not emit a nested Foo::Builder with Build(); it emits a Foo message with typed setters, add_* methods for repeated fields and mutable_* accessors. Treat the message itself as the mutable intermediate, then validate and copy or move it as the product (Foo f; f.set_host("api"); f.add_tags("prod");). The builder-shaped API is generated from the schema, but generated type checks do not enforce domain semantics; keep application validation separate and do not expose mutable message state past the construction boundary.
pitfalls: Wrong move: retain a pointer or reference from mutable_* while continuing to modify the message -> generated accessors may invalidate it -> finish the message before publishing references, or copy the value out.
Wrong move: treat generated setters as semantic validation -> values such as a negative timeout still compile -> validate application invariants before handing the message to consumers.
